newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Hoogovens H1 profit seen up some 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Hoogovens H1 profit seen up some 30 pct.

text.p: Firmer steel and aluminium prices are expected to help Hoogovens NV report a rise in first-half earnings of some 30 percent on Wednesday.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast the metals group's first half net profit from ordinary operations at around 186 million guilders, up from 142 million in the same period of 1996. Individual forecasts range from 162 to 205 million guilders.
Hoogovens' profits dipped in 1996 after a strong 1995, largely because of weaker selling prices.

Analysts noted that aluminium prices had begun to recover in late 1996 and had since stabilised at higher levels, while steel prices had begun to pick up this year, with further price rises due to take effect in the second half of the year.
Hoogovens, which traditionally exports some 10 percent of its steel output across the Atlantic, is also expected to benefit from strong demand and high price levels in the U.S.
The company's continuing cost-reduction efforts are also seen contributing to improved earnings.
Analysts generally see Hoogovens's profits rising further in 1998, assuming Europe's larger economies are poised to recover.
Some see next year as a cyclical peak for the earnings of European steel makers, but others say earnings could remain strong into 1999 if economic recovery endures.
Patrick Rutten at Van Lanschot said it might be time to take profits on Hoogovens shares which rose 74 percent in the seven months to the end of July, while the AEX index rose 52 percent.
The share price, currently around 138 guilders, has already hit price targets adopted by many analysts earlier this year.
"I don't think there is a lot more potential in Hoogovens shares, compared with other cyclical shares," Rutten said.
He currently views paper and packaging group KNP BT as offering greater upside potential, especially if it can find a partner for its paper unit KNP Leykam.
Jeremy Fletcher of CSFB in London said he was withholding his judgement until after the analysts' briefing on the results.
"If the economic upturn continues beyond 1998 into 1999, then you'll see very good cash generation out of (European steel makers) for a protracted period of time," he said.
